name: NY-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+25 partisan lean makes a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely
Claire Valdez has raised $1.7 million with $1.2 million in outside support and no opposition spending
Republican Melvin Rivera shows no reported fundraising or cash on hand
Open seat after Nydia Velázquez's retirement removes incumbent advantage but not the district's lean
model.rationale: The district's D+25 baseline, Valdez's dominant fundraising edge, and prediction markets pricing the Democratic side near 97% all point to a comfortable hold despite the open seat. The Republican nominee's lack of visible fundraising leaves little evidence to move away from the fundamentals.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Valdez or an unexpectedly competitive independent candidacy would be the main signals to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Nydia Velázquez (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Nydia Velázquez's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic Brooklyn-based seat open, but the district's D+25 partisan lean gives the Democratic nominee a large structural advantage. Claire Valdez has raised about $1.7 million and benefits from roughly $1.2 million in outside support, with no recorded spending opposing her. Republican Melvin Rivera reports no fundraising or cash on hand, and an independent candidate has raised only modest sums.

Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97%, consistent with the district's fundamentals. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the forecast rests on the partisan baseline and the money gap, both of which point to a safe Democratic hold.
